xmldoc.short_description: The .nflow model file format, explained (JSON schema reference).

syntax.syntax_item: Reference: the JSON structure of a .nflow model file.

description.p: An nflow model is saved as a single JSON text file with the .nflow extension, encoded in UTF-8. The file is written by save_system and read back by load_system. The editor and the scripted API share the same on-disk layout.

You rarely edit this file by hand, since you build a model with the scripted API (see nflow_build_model) or the editor. Reading it is still useful: it shows how a diagram is represented, which helps you inspect a model, compare two versions in a diff, or generate models from your own code. This page describes the structure one part at a time, then lists every key.

p.b: The structure of a model file

description.p: The root is a JSON object. Its first keys are identity fields: version and format give the schema, metadata records the authoring tool, and name is the model name. Next come the two main arrays: blocks (the boxes) and connections (the wires). Last come the run settings, runtime and sampleTime, which give the duration and the base step. Every model file has this shape: a few identity fields, a list of blocks, a list of wires, and the run settings. The first example below shows a full signal model.
Each entry of blocks is one box on the canvas:

ul.li: id: the block identifier, unique within its (sub)system. This is the name you address in add_line and set_param, so "id": "Gain" is the block you call 'Gain'.
type: the block type, resolved from its library path (for example "gain", "Resistor").
params: the block parameters. The on-canvas label is stored here as "name". Each documented parameter keeps its own name, so a gain of 2 is "Gain": 2.
x, y: the block position on the canvas. rotation is its orientation in degrees.

description.p: Blocks whose port count is explicit may also carry inputs and outputs counts. A subsystem block holds its inner diagram under params.subsystem, which is itself an object with its own blocks and connections arrays. The format nests.

p.b: A signal connection, and port indexing

description.p: Each entry of connections is a signal wire between two blocks of the same (sub)system:

ul.li: from, to: the source and target block ids.
fromIndex, toIndex: the output port and the input port, as a 0-based index.

description.p: Port indices differ between the file and the API. In the file they start at 0; in the scripted API they start at 1. So add_line(model, 'Src/1', 'K/1') (port 1 to port 1) is written in the file as "fromIndex": 0, "toIndex": 0. The file index is the API number minus one. A connection may also carry an optional name (a signal label) and waypoints (the routing geometry the editor draws).

A causal model flows one way, output to input, so a wire has a from and a to. A physical (acausal) model is different: it joins the pins of real components (a resistor's two ends, a mass's flange) into shared points, with no direction. The file records this with a separate top-level array, physicalWires, beside blocks and connections.
Each entry of physicalWires is one node: a set of pins that share a single value (electrical voltage, temperature, or position, with the matching through quantity balanced there).

ul.li: pins: an array of strings, each written "BlockId.pinName" (for example "R1.p", "L1.n", "M1.flange").

description.p: A node always joins two or more pins. Successive add_line calls that share a pin merge into the same node, so a pins array can hold three or more entries. In the acausal example below, ["L1.n", "C1.p", "VS.p"] is one such merged junction. Two further marks of a physical model: the solver is "solver": "dae", and a sensor appears in both arrays, because it has physical pins (in physicalWires) and one signal output (in connections).

ul.li: version: a string, the authoring version (for example "1.0.0").
format: the schema identifier. The current generation is "nflow-2". A missing format is read as the current one, and legacy generations are rejected.
metadata: an object with at least "tool" ("Nelson nflow"), plus optional provenance fields such as "author" and "created".
name: the model name. The loaded model identity is owned by the document and kept stable across edits.
blocks, connections, physicalWires: the arrays described above (the last present only in physical models).
variables: a string of model workspace definitions, empty by default.
runtime: a number, the stop time in seconds (set_param(model, 'StopTime', ...)).
sampleTime: a number, the base sample time in seconds (set_param(model, 'SampleTime', ...)).
solver: a string naming the integration method. Absent (or "discrete") keeps the default fixed-step engine; physical models use "dae".
autoRoute, locked: booleans, whether wires auto-route and whether the diagram is read-only in the editor.

description.p: Optional solver tolerances relTol, absTol and maxStep (set with set_param as RelTol, AbsTol, MaxStep) are stored as numbers when present. The timing fields runtime and sampleTime are stored as JSON numbers, not strings, so the engine honors them.
The excerpts below are annotated; the comments are illustrative and are not part of JSON. The last two examples produce real files you can open and read.
